prompt: Two Chicago physicians described this disease in 1935 in seven patients, and their names stayed on it for the next fifty years. While this disease is one of the most common endocrine disorders in women, there has been a campaign for some time now to rename it again, on the grounds that the current name describes something that is neither always present nor the actual problem.
